1: The function $f$ is given by $f(x)=\begin{cases}2x-3 & \text{for } x<2\\1 & \text{for } 2\le x\le4\end{cases}$. a) Complete the table: for $x=-3$, $x=3$ and a third value of $x$, give $f(x)$, given that the third $f(x)=0$. b) Sketch the graph of function $f$. c) Give all integers $x$ satisfying the inequality $f(x)\ge-6$.
2: Two craftsmen agreed to jointly complete an order of $980$ parts. They planned that each day the first would make $m$ parts and the second $n$ parts. They calculated that together they would complete the order in $7$ days. After the first day of work the first craftsman fell ill, and then the second, in order to complete the whole order (without changing the number of parts made daily), had to work $8$ days longer than planned. Compute $m$ and $n$.
3: The graph of function $f$, given by $f(x)=-2x^2$, is shifted $3$ units right along the $Ox$ axis and $8$ units up along the $Oy$ axis, giving the graph of function $g$. a) Solve the inequality $f(x)+5<3x$. b) Give the range of function $g$. c) The function $g$ is given by the formula $g(x)=-2x^2+bx+c$. Compute $b$ and $c$.
5: The polynomial $W$ is given by $W(x)=x^3+ax^2-4x+b$. a) Determine $a$, $b$ and $c$ so that polynomial $W$ equals polynomial $P$, where $P(x)=x^3+(2a+3)x^2+(a+b+c)x-1$. b) For $a=3$ and $b=0$, write the polynomial $W$ as a product of three first-degree polynomials.
6: The measure of one of the acute angles in a right triangle is equal to $\alpha$. a) Justify that the inequality $\sin\alpha-\tan\alpha<0$ holds. b) For $\sin\alpha=\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}$, compute the value of the expression $\cos^3\alpha+\cos\alpha\cdot\sin^2\alpha$.
7: The arithmetic sequence $(a_n)$, for $n\ge1$, satisfies $a_7=1$ and $a_{11}=9$. a) Compute the first term $a_1$ and the common difference $r$ of the sequence $(a_n)$. b) Check whether the sequence $(a_7,a_8,a_{11})$ is geometric. c) Determine $n$ so that the sum of the first $n$ terms of the sequence $(a_n)$ is the smallest.
8: In trapezoid $ABCD$ the length of base $CD$ is equal to $18$, and the lengths of legs $AD$ and $BC$ are equal to $25$ and $15$ respectively. Angles $ADB$ and $DCB$, marked in the figure, have equal measures [Figure: trapezoid ABCD with the given side lengths and the two marked equal angles]. Compute the perimeter of this trapezoid.
9: Points $B=(0,10)$ and $O=(0,0)$ are vertices of right triangle $OAB$, in which $|\angle OAB|=90°$. Leg $OA$ lies on the line with equation $y=\frac{1}{2}x$. Compute the coordinates of point $A$ and the length of leg $OA$.
10: A table shows the results of the theoretical part of a driving-license exam. A candidate passed if they made at most two mistakes. Number of mistakes: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8; number of candidates: 8,5,8,5,2,1,0,0,1 respectively. a) Compute the arithmetic mean of the number of mistakes made by the candidates, rounded to a whole number. b) Compute the probability that, among two randomly chosen candidates, exactly one passed. Give the result as an irreducible fraction.
11: The lateral surface of a cylinder, unrolled onto a plane, is a rectangle. The diagonal of this rectangle has length $12$ and forms a $30°$ angle with the side whose length equals the height of the cylinder. a) Compute the lateral surface area of this cylinder. b) Check whether the volume of this cylinder is greater than $18\sqrt3$. Justify your answer.
